trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.summary: Following the v2.3.1 deployment, checkout-api failed health checks (error rate ~18%). Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release healthy in production. The first rollback attempt partially failed (orchestrator error halted rollout after us-east); a retry completed the rollout to the remaining regions (us-west, eu-west). All regions are now running v2.3.0 and the service is healthy (error rate ~0.2%).
args.title: checkout-api rolled back to v2.3.0 after unhealthy v2.3.1 deploy

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Identified the bad release**: The latest deploy, **v2.3.1**, was unhealthy in production. The most recent healthy production release was **v2.3.0**.
2. **Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0**: The first rollback attempt only completed in us-east before halting with an orchestrator error. I verified the state (us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1), then retried — the retry completed the rollout to all regions.
3. **Verified recovery**: checkout-api is now healthy across us-east, us-west, and eu-west, all on v2.3.0, with the error rate down from ~18% to ~0.2%.
4. **Opened a SEV2 incident** (INC-0001) documenting the bad deploy, the partial rollback failure, the retry, and the recovery. The incident creation API returned a timeout, but checking the incident list confirmed it was created successfully — no duplicate was opened.

Note: no change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production.
